The eight behaviour features of each respondent

Source: R/behaviour.R
behaviour_features.Rd

behaviour_features() describes how each respondent answers, apart from what they answer. The eight features are the building blocks of the Behaviour index in synthetic_behaviour() and of the careless flags in flag_careless().

Usage

behaviour_features(data, items, real = NULL, fit_scales = NULL)

Arguments

data

a data frame of responses (one row per respondent, items as columns, matched by name to items$item).

items

a data frame with one row per item: item (column name), scale (or trait, as in hexaco_items), an optional facet and an optional logical reverse.

real

optional data frame of real responses used as the reference (see Details). NULL uses data.

fit_scales

the scales used for person fit. NULL uses all scales; character(0) skips person fit (the person_fit column is then NA).

Value

A tibble with one row per respondent of data and the eight feature columns.

Details

FeatureDefinitionCareless side
variabilitySD of the raw answers across all itemsVery low or very high
extremeShare of answers at the lowest or highest categoryHigh
midpointShare of answers at the middle category (odd number of categories only)High
acquiescenceMean raw answer minus the scale midpointHigh
key_inconsistencyMean over facets of the absolute difference between the keyed means of the positive and the reverse-keyed itemsHigh
even_oddCorrelation across facets between the keyed means of the odd-numbered and the even-numbered items of each facetLow
mahalanobisSquare root of the Mahalanobis distance of the keyed facet means, using the real data's mean and covarianceHigh
person_fitStandardized log-likelihood \(l_z\) (Drasgow) under a graded response model fitted to the real data, one model per scale, averaged over scalesLow (misfit); very high means "too coherent"

Keying. Keyed answers recode reverse-keyed items as (min + max) - x, where min and max are the lowest and highest answers in the reference data (for HEXACO: 8 - x). Variability, Extreme, Midpoint and Acquiescence use the raw answers.

Reference. The facet means and covariance for mahalanobis and the graded response models for person_fit come from real (from data itself when real is NULL). The models are fitted once per scale with mirt::mirt(real_keyed[scale_items], 1, "graded") and are never refitted on synthetic data. Every respondent gets the MAP theta on a grid of 81 points from -5 to 5 with a standard normal prior, and \(l_z\) is computed at that theta. Answers in a category that the real data never use count as missing for person fit.

Facets. Without a facet column, the scales stand in for facets in key_inconsistency, even_odd and mahalanobis. even_odd needs at least three facets with two or more items.

Missing answers. A feature is NA for a respondent who answered fewer than half of the items it needs (all items, or a scale's items for person fit).

See also

synthetic_behaviour(), flag_careless()

Examples

h <- hexaco_items[hexaco_items$trait == "H", ]
real <- hexaco_real[hexaco_real$country == "Canada", ]
syn <- hexaco_llm[hexaco_llm$country == "Canada" & hexaco_llm$attempt == 1, ]
f <- behaviour_features(syn[1:200, ], h, real = real, fit_scales = character(0))
summary(f)
#>   variability       extreme          midpoint       acquiescence    
#>  Min.   :1.163   Min.   :0.0000   Min.   :0.0500   Min.   :-0.7250  
#>  1st Qu.:1.535   1st Qu.:0.0500   1st Qu.:0.1250   1st Qu.:-0.5250  
#>  Median :1.768   Median :0.1500   Median :0.1500   Median :-0.4500  
#>  Mean   :1.690   Mean   :0.1265   Mean   :0.1444   Mean   :-0.3149  
#>  3rd Qu.:1.840   3rd Qu.:0.2000   3rd Qu.:0.1562   3rd Qu.:-0.0500  
#>  Max.   :1.987   Max.   :0.2500   Max.   :0.2750   Max.   : 0.5500  
#>                                                                     
#>  key_inconsistency    even_odd       mahalanobis      person_fit 
#>  Min.   :0.2562    Min.   :0.5915   Min.   :1.204   Min.   : NA  
#>  1st Qu.:0.3809    1st Qu.:0.9060   1st Qu.:1.600   1st Qu.: NA  
#>  Median :0.4458    Median :0.9494   Median :1.690   Median : NA  
#>  Mean   :0.5013    Mean   :0.9327   Mean   :1.691   Mean   :NaN  
#>  3rd Qu.:0.5611    3rd Qu.:0.9744   3rd Qu.:1.763   3rd Qu.: NA  
#>  Max.   :1.0479    Max.   :0.9994   Max.   :2.295   Max.   : NA  
#>                                                     NAs    :200  
# \donttest{
# with person fit (fits a graded response model to the real data)
f <- behaviour_features(syn[1:200, ], h, real = real)
summary(f$person_fit)
#>    Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max. 
#>   0.946   1.406   1.563   1.617   1.781   2.745 
# }
